newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends higher, soyoil lower.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends higher, soyoil lower.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures ended higher on Tuesday, taking cues from the July contract which went off the board firm, traders said.

"The July was strong all morning," one veteran oilseeds trader said. "Beans took a hit after Continental delivered but meal managed to hold on. I think the trade was impressed by that. It shows the nearby demand is still there."
No meal deliveries have been posted against the July but there were two million bushels of soybeans posted on Tuesday.
Nearby months also closed higher, in tandem with soybeans which rose amid talk of export demand.

Traders also pointed to long-range forecasts which suggested another hot, dry spell for portions of the U.S. Midwest this weekend. Last week's hot weather contributed to declines in crop conditions, traders said.
USDA Monday said 62 percent of the soybean crop was rated good to excellent as of Sunday, down from 66 last week.
Soyoil struggled with abundant supplies and only routine export business.
Soymeal ended $2.50 to $0.10 per ton higher with December up $2.00 at $195.70. Soyoil closed 0.20 to 0.10 cent per lb lower with December down 0.18 at 22.11.

On the day, Smith Barney sold 500 lots August soymeal, 300 lots December and 200 lots September, pit sources said. Iowa Grain sold 200 August and 100 December and Griffin Trading bought 200 August, pit sources said.
In soyoil, Refco Inc and Merrill Lynch each sold 200 December and Produce Grain bought 400 December and 100 September, traders said.

Crush spreading was active with Central Soya said to be spreading 500,000 bushels August at 42 to 43 cents. Produce Grain, Cargill Investor Services and Tenco Inc were also said to be crush spreaders in the August.
Traders pointed to strengthening crush margins. CBOT on Tuesday put August crush margins at 43.88 cents a bushel, up 2.32 cents from Monday.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 22,000 lots, compared with Monday's actual volume of 23,932 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 10,000 lots, against Monday's 13,300.
